notes.text: The opening paragraph says that the bouchage operations are relatively superficial: at fixed g they do not relate the indicated objects to ones with smaller g. It points instead to erasing the cutting circles, labelled by the source’s raised circled 5°. The written numeral is retained; no cross-page renumbering is imported from H’s editorial note.

The next paragraph asks to make explicit the fundamental groupoids Pi_1(X;R) of the displayed triples, with the nonempty base-point condition and functorial dependence on R. The short form p^ts-base is preserved. The curved condition leader fixes its attachment after the baseline base-point phrase, while en tant que remains baseline text.

The rewritten passage speaks of every finite-set representation of the groupoid, an associated covering X-prime of X, and a new object of the displayed S T category. The author says that the question is already nontrivial for S_2 T_{0,3}, then calls the demand perhaps too ambitious. The page ends at car, leaving that reason unfinished. The cancelled predecessor, initial letters of the raised defining phrase, and de/des remain explicitly uncertain.

The margin says that the displayed, decoratively doubtful Sigma datum ne joue aucun rôle and proposes working in S T_top^± instead of S T D_top^±. This supersedes the first reading’s formally-empty wording. The cancelled predecessor of rôle and the compressed middle phrase remain doubtful. The two category names and au lieu de were read directly; H’s inclusion symbol is unsupported. The larger groupoïdes on the right of the margin crop belongs to the main paragraph and is not repeated in the note.

Three long curved strokes function as attachment leaders under raised additions: Pi_1(X;R), the nonempty condition, and the defining phrase. The completed audit distinguishes those leader strokes from separately visible opening parentheses before en tant que and d’un, which are retained. The literal opening square bracket before the defining phrase is retained without an invented closing bracket; the source closing parentheses after opération and X also remain.

Every agreed main word and formula was compared on the original and prepared halves, then all differing words and resolved C doubts were inspected on enlarged crops. The original and each half were displayed once. Seventeen distinct places produced nineteen saved and actually viewed evidence files; the two additional files are targeted extensions of the still-open margin, not rereadings of settled text. No OCR, web reference or TeX compilation was used.

The initial five-image crop-view attempt returned a wholly truncated result, with no displayed image available for inspection. Those images were then successfully displayed in smaller batches; the nineteen recorded views count actual inspections, not the failed output. The pale lower 63 is recorded without attributing its hand.

The preceding operations list on scan 061 labels erasing cutting circles as 4, while this leaf explicitly gives the raised circled 5°. The clear numeral is preserved as a cross-reference mismatch rather than silently harmonized. The insertion state of that unchanged numeral, the empty-set glyph form, and the abbreviation are not counted as changes of mathematical content.

The independent reading exposed a material error in the margin: the ink says that the Sigma datum ne joue aucun role, not that it est formellement vide. The live role is clear; its cancelled predecessor and the compressed following phrase remain doubtful. This affects the interpretation of why the author proposes working in S T-top instead of S T D-top, but it is not a proof of an equivalence. Opening parentheses before en tant que and d'un are restored after separating their curves from the insertion leaders. The abbreviated tte and par ens finis are confirmed from the strokes, as are the singular nouvelle operation and groupoide. The phi-shaped empty-set glyph remains as written. All thirteen unequal boxes were viewed after the complete independent TSV was frozen.

audit_changes.evidence: The lower cancelled group has a low u/n run and an e-like final turn. The heavy strike hides enough of the interiors that une is now retained with avec as an alternative. The raised en and the long l of liaison are distinct. This is a certainty change, not a newly counted word correction.; crops/148_scan064_second_B05.png

After the two tall l loops of celle, the live article has a d ascender, e loop and a final pointed downward turn supporting des. The following low group is under the strike; une remains primary, with des unresolved. No grammatical correction to du is made.; crops/148_scan064_second_B07.png

The whole tuple and the raised Pi-one expression were viewed. The middle glyph has a lower horizontal base and angular return, like the recurring Sigma, rather than an independently clear R leg. Its short upper decoration and the bracket overlap, so tilde-Sigma/plain-Sigma remain doubtful. The low article beneath the leader is compatible with the existing des.; crops/148_scan064_second_B08.png

The raised condition was also viewed in a boundary extension containing its complete glyph. It has a small oval crossed by a long oblique stem, retained as the manuscript phi-shaped empty-set sign. The abbreviation has a full-height p and small raised ts, followed by a hyphen. A long opening curve before en is visible and is restored as the opening parenthesis. The insertion leader extends to the right above this curve.; crops/148_scan064_second_B09.png

The two l loops of nouvelle are followed by one e exit. Operation has its p descender, accent, t stem and compressed ion ending. Neither word has a distinct added final s before the large closing parenthesis, so the singular reading remains.; crops/148_scan064_second_B11.png

Two adjacent tall strokes joined by a crossbar and a separate low e give tte, not la/de. The raised representation word is readable. The old lower word is heavily crossed; its reconstitution proposal remains under doubt rather than being replaced by an entirely illegible token.; crops/148_scan064_second_B12.png

The main crop shows par with a p descender and low a/r, then the low e/n/s abbreviation, followed by f, two dotted i strokes and the nis ending of finis. These are not pour une fois. A boundary extension shows the opening d loop and low u run; no separate apostrophe is visible. The existing du groupoide par ens finis is retained.; crops/148_scan064_second_B13.png

An opening square bracket precedes the raised crowded word. Its tall f-like stroke and dotted continuation admit definissant/definition, and the last short group admits un/du. A second, thinner curved stroke beside the insertion leader precedes the baseline d-apostrophe-un; the opening parenthesis is restored, while no invented closing square bracket is added.; crops/148_scan064_second_B14.png

The singular revetement has a short accent stroke above e; the conventional French circumflex is retained rather than adding an accent-shape doubt. X-prime is raised. The d before X has a long terminal exit whose hook may contain s, so de/des is not resolved on this crop.; crops/148_scan064_second_B15.png

The opening article has a looped d followed by a low u. Groupoide ends in a d ascender and e exit without an independent s. The cancelled category remains too overworked to resolve. S has the ordinary two curved turns, whereas T has a looped head; the calligraphic-S wrapper is not a different source reading.; crops/148_scan064_second_B16.png

The formula shows S with subscript 2, loop-headed T and subscripts 0,3. The S-versus-calligraphic-S distinction is editorial styling only; the established source reading is retained.; crops/148_scan064_second_B17.png

audit_changes.evidence: The rotated whole margin and existing enlarged middle crop were viewed. After ici are two low joined strokes ne; the next line begins a long j descender followed by oue and then the low aucun group. The following live word has an accent over o and a tall l: role, not vide. A preceding old role-like group is crossed and remains doubtful. Autant is readable, but bien/dire/donc and the short phrase before mettre remain uncertain. The next lines retain mettre dans les and a c-opening cas/corps proposal. The lower preposition before the category has a low s/u/r run without a tall d and now reads sur. The two categories and au lieu de survive; neighbouring large main-line writing is not imported into this margin. The upper Sigma decoration may be a flattened tilde or bar and is not resolved.; crops/148_scan064_second_B18.png
The lower isolated folio has a closed-loop 6 and the two lobes of 3. Both readings are 63; mspage and margin differ only in editorial wrapper.; crops/148_scan064_second_B19.png
